headline: A second court turned down one exchange visitor's request about the fixed admission period rule
plain: On September 14, 2026, a federal court in the District of Columbia turned down a request from one exchange visitor. She had asked that the fixed admission period rule not apply to her while her case goes on. Her case is about a waiver, not the rule, and the ruling covers only that case. The same day, a court in Boston put off the start of the rule itself.

source_label.agency: U.S. District Court, District of Columbia

claims.text: The plaintiffs in Trilleras Gomez v. Mullin, No. 1:26-cv-02364 (D.D.C.), asked the court to keep the final rule of July 17, 2026 from applying to one J-1 plaintiff while the case goes on.
claims.quote: Plaintiffs seek to enjoin a new Department of Homeland Security (DHS) rule from applying to Trilleras for the duration of this litigation.

claims.text: The plaintiffs do not challenge the final rule itself; their lawsuit is about a waiver of the J-1 two year home residence requirement.
claims.quote: Plaintiffs bring no independent challenge to the September Rule.

claims.text: The court denied the motion for a preliminary injunction in an opinion dated September 14, 2026.
claims.quote: For the foregoing reasons, Plaintiffs’ motion for a preliminary injunction, ECF 8, is DENIED.

claims.text: On the same day the District of Massachusetts (No. 1:26-cv-13799, ECF 51) postponed the effective date of the final rule, not only for the parties to that case.
claims.quote: The effective date of the Final Rule is hereby POSTPONED pending further order of this court or resolution of this proceeding on the merits.

history.note: The District of Columbia denied one J-1 plaintiff's motion for a preliminary injunction (ECF 14). The District of Massachusetts postponed the rule the same day (ECF 51).
